findings.title: Restart leaves stale SpansBuffer and doesn't kill thread/old process safely
findings.body: On restart, _create_process_for_shards builds a new SpansBuffer and replaces self.buffers[process_index]. The old process is killed only if it is a multiprocessing.Process, so in thread mode (tests) a hung thread keeps running alongside the new one. Both threads then flush the same shards and can produce duplicate segments. Also, kill() is not followed by join(), so the old process may not have exited before the new one starts.

findings.title: join() deadline handling can leave later processes unterminated
findings.body: When the deadline expires, the loop breaks before reaching the remaining processes. Those processes are never terminate()d and keep running as orphans until the daemon flag takes effect. Terminate should happen for every process regardless of the deadline. In addition, `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None` treats timeout=0 as no deadline, so join waits forever.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag names
findings.body: The produce timer and segment_size_bytes use the tag "shard", but wait_produce uses "shards". Dashboards that aggregate by tag will split or miss data. The _ensure_processes_alive metric also tags a single "shard" per shard in the process, which makes it count N times for a shared process.

findings.title: Unused helper and shared stopped value set to True
findings.body: _create_process_for_shard is dead code. terminate() sets the shared `stopped` Value (type "i") to True without joining or killing the child processes. This is relatively minor.
